methods.title: At the photocopier
methods.prompt: {source} is at the photocopier, waiting for it to warm up. It will be a while, and you could ask about anyone.
frames: The photocopier jams, and you and {source} stand looking at it. "Have you been here long enough to know about this?" {source} says, meaning the machine, and then does not mean the machine. "{said}"
{source} is copying something face down, and shifts slightly so that you cannot read it. "While you're there," {source} says. "{said}"
You ask how the week is going. {source} says fine, looks over one shoulder and carries on more quietly. "{said}"
You mention the name, as if it had just occurred to you. {source} presses a button that does nothing. "Funny you should say that. {said}"

methods.title: At the loading bay
methods.prompt: A coffee, a favour, an agreement not to mention something. Only two people on this floor sell, and they sell secrets.
frames: You hand {source} a coffee. {source} takes off the lid, looks at it for a while and seems to find it acceptable. "{said}"
{source} lets you stand there for some time, then takes the coffee. "You didn't get this from me. {said}"
"That's a large coffee," says {source}, looking across the yard and not at you. "All right. {said}"

motives.text: {name} was keeping out of trouble, and told you whatever would achieve that.
{name} had an eye on your job, and any confusion on your part was welcome.
{name} was glad that anyone had asked, and did not want the conversation to end.
{name} wanted nothing from you, which on this floor is unusual.

believer: Have you seen the values statement? {subject} has. Properly, with a pen.
{subject} was here until nine on Tuesday, and nobody had even asked. I don't think it's for show. I did check.
I told {subject} the numbers were a bit off, and {subject} went and fixed them. Who does that?
incompetent: Honestly, ask {subject} what this department does. Go on. I'd like to watch.
{subject} has been sending round the same spreadsheet since the spring. Nobody has the heart.
Lovely, {subject}. Really lovely. I wouldn't let {subject} near a budget, mind.
practitioner: You'll have noticed {subject} is never in the room when something goes wrong. That takes planning.
{subject} has been very nice to you, hasn't {subject}? Yes. I'd keep a note of what for.
I've seen {subject} remember a birthday. It was the birthday of someone's boss.

high: If you want something decided, you'd go to {subject}. Never mind what the chart says.
Funny, isn't it, how people stop talking when {subject} walks in.
I saw that plan before it went upstairs. {subject} had already been through it in pencil.
low: Bless {subject}. Still gets invited to things. Doesn't get told what happened at them.
People nod at {subject}, and then they go and ask someone else.
{subject} thinks that project is still {subject}'s. Nobody has worked out how to say.

true.label: True
true.note: It was so. Whether that did you any good is another matter.

mistaken.label: Mistaken
mistaken.note: Your source believed every word of it.

outOfDate.label: Out of date
outOfDate.note: It was so, two reorganisations ago.

false.label: Deliberately false
false.note: Your source knew otherwise, and chose this.
